candidates.title: The Bridge That Rose Without Rain
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the floating footbridge lifted sharply each afternoon despite steady river levels before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they added ballast but the bridge still rose unevenly; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized air trapped beneath a repair pontoon expanded in the afternoon heat; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they vented the pontoon safely and installed a pressure relief fitting, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Melody That Led Travelers Astray
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered visitors following musical trail markers repeatedly reached the wrong clearing before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they repainted the arrows but the detour persisted; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized two different chimes produced identical notes when heard across the valley; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they retuned one marker and added visible route symbols, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.

candidates.title: The Snow Beacon That Changed Color
story_beats: At the snowy meadow, rabbit and fox discovered the mountain beacon appeared green from one trail and red from another before the library opened, leaving the visiting readers waiting.
Rabbit attempted an immediate fix, but they replaced its colored cover but the contradiction remained; fox stopped the attempt before the situation worsened.
Fox examined the evidence and realized a wedge of clear ice split the light differently across viewing angles; together they revised their plan rather than repeating the mistake.
With the visiting readers watching, they cleared the ice and added a protective hood while verifying both trails, then explained the clue so their neighbors could prevent the problem next time.
